voices.note: anonymous redactorial voice; narrator of the maasim, asks וכמה כל צורכו and בבבל היכא, and says הני מילי
eulogizes at 28b.10; his dictum on the daughters of Israel is quoted by Reish Lakish at 28b.16
the man who carried Reish Lakish across the water (28b.15-16)
תנו רבנן (28b.18-29a.1): one interrupts Torah study for the dead and the bride
whose practice the baraita reports (אמרו עליו)
subject of both versions of the כל-צורכו measure; commits nothing directly
transmits in Rav's name (משמיה דרב), version 1
ואמרי לה -- the variant tradition reporting version 2 of Rav's measure
Shmuel's father, with Levi, in the maaseh at 29a.5
the Holy One, who says שבקוהו in the Rav Sheshet maaseh (29a.6)
King David, speaker of Ps 26:8 as Abaye cites it (דקאמר דוד)
the heavenly voice inside Bar Kappara's derasha (29a.10)

props.gloss_en: Rafram eulogized his daughter-in-law in the synagogue
Rafram: because of my honour and the deceased's, everyone will come
R' Zeira eulogized a certain sage in the synagogue
R' Zeira: whether because of my honour or because of the deceased's, everyone will come
Reish Lakish eulogized a young scholar, found in the Land of Israel, who studied halakha in the twenty-fourth row
Reish Lakish: alas, the Land of Israel has lost a great man
Rav Nachman, asked to eulogize one who had studied halakha, Sifra, Sifrei and Tosefta: how shall I eulogize him -- 'alas, a basket full of books is lost'?!
come and see the difference between the harsh ones of the Land of Israel and the pious ones of Babylonia
the mishna (Avot): and one who makes use of the crown perishes
Reish Lakish taught: this is one who makes use of one who studies halakhot, the crown of Torah
Ulla: a man may make use of one who studies four [orders]
Ulla: and he may not make use of one who teaches four
Reish Lakish was going on the road and reached a pool of water; a man came, set him on his shoulders and was carrying him across
the man, asked by Reish Lakish: I have read [Scripture]; I have studied four orders of mishna
Reish Lakish: you have hewn four mountains, and you carry bar Lakish on your shoulder?! throw bar Lakish into the water!
the man: it pleases me to serve the master
Reish Lakish: if so, learn from me this matter that R' Zeira said
the daughters of Israel were strict on themselves: even if they see a drop of blood like a mustard seed, they sit seven clean days for it
whoever studies halakhot is assured that he is of the world to come
as it is said, 'His ways (halichot) are eternal' (Hab 3:6) -- do not read halichot but halachot
one interrupts Torah study to carry out the dead
and to bring in a bride
they said of R' Yehuda b. R' Ilai that he would interrupt Torah study to carry out the dead and to bring in a bride
in what case is this said? where there are not there all that is needed
but where there are there all that is needed, one does not interrupt
and how many is 'all that is needed'?
Rav (version 1): twelve thousand men, and six thousand horns
Rav (version 2, ואמרי לה): twelve thousand men, of whom six thousand [carry] horns
Ulla: for example, where men are lined up from the town gate to the burial place
Rav Sheshet: as its [the Torah's] giving, so its taking
Rav Sheshet: as its giving was with six hundred thousand, so its taking is with six hundred thousand
these words [the measures] apply to one who read and studied
but for one who taught, there is no measure
come and see how beloved Israel is before the Holy One: wherever they were exiled, the Shechina was with them
they were exiled to Egypt -- the Shechina was with them
as it is said, 'did I reveal Myself to your father's house when they were in Egypt' (I Sam 2:27)
they were exiled to Babylonia -- the Shechina was with them
as it is said, 'for your sake I have sent to Babylonia' (Isa 43:14)
and also when they are to be redeemed, the Shechina is with them
as it is said, 'and the Lord your God will return (veshav) your captivity' (Deut 30:3): it does not say veheshiv but veshav -- teaching that the Holy One returns with them from among the exiles
in Babylonia, where [is the Shechina]?
Abaye: in the synagogue of Huzal, and in the synagogue of Shaf veYativ in Nehardea
and do not say here and here [at once], but sometimes here and sometimes here
Abaye: may [blessing] come to me, for when I am a parasang away, I go in and pray there
Shmuel's father and Levi were sitting in the synagogue of Shaf veYativ in Nehardea; the Shechina came, they heard a sound of tumult, rose and left
Rav Sheshet was sitting in the synagogue of Shaf veYativ in Nehardea; the Shechina came and he did not leave; the ministering angels came and were frightening him
Rav Sheshet before Him: Master of the world, one wretched and one not wretched -- who yields to whom?
He said to them: leave him
'and I was to them a small sanctuary' (Ezek 11:16) -- R' Yitzchak: these are the synagogues and study halls in Babylonia
and R' Elazar said: this is the house of our master in Babylonia
Rava expounded: what is written, 'Lord, You have been a dwelling (maon) for us' (Ps 90:1)? these are the synagogues and study halls
Abaye: at first I used to study at home and pray in the synagogue
Abaye: once I heard what David says, 'Lord, I love the dwelling (meon) of Your house' (Ps 26:8), I studied in the synagogue
the reason for Abaye's change: David's 'Lord, I love the dwelling of Your house' (Ps 26:8)
David: 'Lord, I love the dwelling of Your house' (Ps 26:8)
R' Elazar HaKappar: the synagogues and study halls in Babylonia are destined to be fixed in the Land of Israel
as it is said, 'surely as Tabor among the mountains, and as Carmel by the sea, he shall come' (Jer 46:18)
Bar Kappara expounded 'why do you look askance (teratzdun), high-peaked mountains' (Ps 68:17): a bat kol went out and said to them, why do you seek (tirtzu) judgement (din) with Sinai?
the bat kol: you are all blemished beside Sinai
Rav Ashi: learn from this that one who is arrogant is blemished

schemas.gloss_en: ומה תבור וכרמל שלא באו אלא לפי שעה ללמוד תורה נקבעים בארץ ישראל, בתי כנסיות ובתי מדרשות שקורין ומרביצין בהן תורה -- על אחת כמה וכמה: if Tabor and Carmel, which came only for a moment to learn Torah, are fixed in the Land, synagogues and study halls where Torah is read and spread all the more so
כתיב הכא ״גבנונים״ וכתיב התם ״או גבן או דק״ -- 'high-peaked' of the mountains is the 'hunchback' of the priestly blemishes (Lev 21:20): the mountains are blemished

supports.gloss_en: שמע מינה -- from the bat kol's calling the mountains blemished, one who is arrogant is blemished (kind svara: no support kind names שמע מינה; that the mountains were arrogant in demanding the Torah is Steinsaltz's explanation, not the text's)
